chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Hama, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Clip the nails, for they are the resting-place of the Satan, and from them comes forgetfulness.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical wisdom behind clipping nails in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of grooming to spiritual hygiene, identifying the nails as a 'dwelling place' (*maqil*) for Satan, which impedes mental clarity. This explanation underscores the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition), where maintaining bodily purity is seen as essential for preserving cognitive function and preventing the forgetfulness (*nisyān*) often associated with spiritual neglect.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Ayoub Bin Al Hurr, from Abu Hama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘But rather, clip the nails because these are a resting-place for the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and from it happens the forgetfulness’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from those whom he has mentioned from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
’There is clipping of fingernails; it reduces Satan; and because of it (unclipped fingernails) is forgetfulness.’”
